assumptions: EditR's (Kluesner et al. 2018) zero-adjusted gamma model of background noise.
limits: One trace, no control; edits outside the guide window are not scored.
bio.jane/contract.question: What fraction of each base in the guide window was edited, from one trace (EditR)?

description: Quantify BASE EDITING from a single Sanger trace, with no control read — the EditR method (Kluesner et al. 2018), ported and graded against the authors' own R. A base editor makes no double-strand break and no indel, so it is invisible to ICE and TIDE: the edit is a C→T or A→G inside the protospacer that shows up only as a second peak under the called base. This models the trace's OWN background from the positions outside the guide, then p-values every base of the guide against it. Emits the significant calls, so a pipeline can gate on whether editing happened and at which position.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

document.description: which trace file to read: its name (`read_F.ab1`) or its project file id. LEAVE IT EMPTY to run on the chromatogram tab that is open. A file id is project-specific, so a template ships this unset.

guide.description: the protospacer, 5'→3', without the PAM. Matched exactly against the read's own base calls; the coordinates it lands on come back in the result.

guide_end.description: the other end of an explicit placement, 1-based inclusive. Pair it with `guide_start`.

guide_is_reverse_complement.description: search for the guide's reverse complement. A C→T edit on the guide strand then reads as G→A in the result.

guide_start.description: place the guide yourself, 1-based inclusive in the read's own base calls, instead of matching it exactly. GIVE BOTH BOUNDS OR NEITHER. This is what a read carrying a sequencing error inside the protospacer needs: the analysis tests the bases you point at rather than refusing the read.

p_value_cutoff.description: a base is called as edited when its share of the position's signal clears this trace's own noise model at this probability. EditR's own default is 0.01.

trim3.description: last base of the read the background model may be fitted on, 1-based inclusive. Pair it with `trim5`.

trim5.description: first base of the read the background model may be fitted on, 1-based inclusive. GIVE BOTH BOUNDS OR NEITHER — upstream errors on a lone one rather than filling the other in. Left unset, upstream's automatic rule runs: drop the first 20 bases, then drop every base whose total peak height is under a tenth of the mean of what is left. The window is an INPUT to the answer, not a view: it is what the noise is estimated from, so tightening it lowers the cut-off.

name: quantify_base_editing

calls.description: every significant call: { guidePosition, index, guideBase, base, percent, pValue }, biggest first

edited.description: whether ANY base of the guide carries a non-reference signal above this trace's own noise. Wire it into a gate

guideStart.description: 1-based position in the read's own base calls where the guide was found — what a canvas needs to draw it

report.description: the whole run: every guide position with all four base percentages and p-values, the four fitted noise models and their cut-off lines. This is what makes a negative checkable — 'no editing' and 'the model could never have fired' look identical without it

topChange.description: the biggest call as `reference→edited`, e.g. `C→T`. Empty when there is none

topPercent.description: its share of that position's total peak height, 0–100

topPosition.description: the guide position (1-based) of the biggest call, or 0 when there is none
